modelDescription: The moment people, tools and records stop agreeing with each other.
title: Start with the work, not the feature list.
description: I go looking for the repeated handoff, the state nobody wrote down, and the exact moment someone stops trusting the record and reaches for their phone instead.
example: Hibah began with a donor programme run out of a spreadsheet and a WhatsApp group. That gap was the brief.

modelDescription: Entities, state, boundaries, and every way it can go wrong.
title: Give the messy parts hard edges.
description: Domain models, permissions, state transitions and failure modes should make the system easier to explain to the person running it. If it takes a diagram to defend, the model is wrong.
example: PumpOS pins shifts, stock, credit and reporting to a single business-day record. One day, one truth.

modelDescription: APIs, data, interfaces, and a way to hear back from the system.
title: Pick the tool for the constraint in front of you.
description: Go when the service needs to be small and fast. Flutter when one codebase has to reach every screen. TypeScript for the web. Swift when it should feel native on a Mac. No loyalty, only fit.
example: tqwp is a small Go API for running concurrent work with retries you can actually configure.

modelDescription: Then learn from what the system meets in the real world.
title: Own the path until a person can use it.
description: A clean backend that never meets a user is a hobby. Quality shows up after contact with product behaviour, deployment, and a Tuesday afternoon with bad connectivity.
example: Live products, public repositories, and an extension submitted to Raycast. All of it is out there to be judged.
